items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from the greeting into probing questions with no roadmap for the call
Never used the customer's name once in a 16-minute call — she volunteered 'Debbie Myers' in her opening line and he never picked it up or used it, including at the farewell where she used his

No Worries Damage Coverage never pitched — no mention of the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse coverage, despite the customer raising liability twice (pod loading waiver, dresser-drawer waiver). He said 'insurance' was included in the hourly rate and stopped there
'No deposit required' never stated — a key differentiator on a call where the customer said she has one more bid to collect

Save Your Ass prep speech never delivered — no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip. Customer explicitly asked to be priced both with and without packing, so the self-pack scenario applied. When prep did come up he framed it as cost-neutral ('it ultimately comes out to the same cost'), which is the opposite of the section's point

Never quoted the without-packing option she explicitly asked for — he described how the estimate would be split across two days but only ever stated the packing-inclusive totals ($2,766 + $3,270 = $6,036)
Origin stairs/floors never probed — customer mentioned 'a bookcase with books upstairs' at Bellingham but later described it as 'a single story house'; the contradiction went uncaught and unpriced
Origin parking/access never probed (destination access was probed well)
Steps at the front of the destination home were raised by the customer but never factored into the estimate as a time variable
Walk-distance variable never explained, despite alley parking and a route through the garage or backyard at the destination
No equivalents or comparison anchors (school bus reference, etc.) used to make the time estimate concrete
Booking attempt was passive — 'If you wanted to save the spot, I could send that as well... I'm happy to follow your lead on that.' No direct ask to lock in Sept 4-5
Email handoff mentioned but never explained — no bolded key-details list at the top, no 'reply with any corrections'
Business hours never given; the customer had to ask who her point of contact would be rather than being told proactively
Discount request ('offer any veteran discounts?') answered with a flat 'unfortunately we don't' and no value reframe — and the prior-military disclosure that followed was never acknowledged

Direct question 'how many guys did you say you send to pack?' got a fragmentary answer — the crew count was never actually restated, and he had already given two different numbers (five movers as the typical, four in her quote)
top_strength: The pricing and clock walkthrough was genuinely excellent — he built the estimate out loud with transparent math ($109/hr per mover, 4 movers, 6 hrs pack + 7.5 hrs move + $150 materials = $6,036), explained that materials are the only line outside the hourly rate and that unused boxes aren't charged, and closed with 'you're charged only for time used' plus a sense-check. He also handled two genuinely unusual asks — loading a third-party pod and moving loaded dressers — by explaining the liability waiver clearly instead of just saying no, and correctly declined the 1,200 lb Liberty safe on safe-working-load grounds.
coaching_note: This customer told you flat out she was taking your numbers to her husband and getting one more bid — and you gave her nothing but a price to compare. All four Einstein differentiators went unsaid: No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and no deposit. That's the worst possible call to leave them out of, because the competitor's quote will be a number too, and a number is the only thing she can weigh. The No Worries miss is the sharpest one — she brought up liability herself twice (the pod waiver and the dresser drawers), and both times you explained what Einstein does NOT cover without ever telling her what it DOES. Then you closed with 'I'm happy to follow your lead on that' instead of asking for Sept 4-5. Next call: when a customer signals they're comparison shopping, that's the trigger to run the full differentiator block, state 'no deposit to hold the date,' and then actually ask for the booking.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and competent through a complicated scenario and the customer left satisfied ('that was very quick and easy'), but the warmth was generic — zero name use, no humor or rapport, filler acknowledgments like 'Alright' and 'Perfect' between topics, and the 'we're prior military, we've moved multiple times' disclosure was an open rapport door he walked straight past.
